chunks: Sa'd narrated from Abu Ja'far, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn 'Umara, who said:

I sent to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) asking him about a man: is his prayer of the obligatory prayer alone in the mosque of Kufa better, or his prayer in congregation better? He said, 'Prayer in congregation is better.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (Imam Musa al-Kadhim's son, often referred to as al-Rida)

ai.seo_question: Is it better to pray the obligatory prayer alone or in congregation according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the jurisprudential preference for congregational prayer over individual prayer, even within the prestigious setting of Kufa's mosque. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on communal unity (*jamāʿah*) and the social dimension of worship, reinforcing the Prophet’s tradition that congregational prayer holds greater merit due to the collective presence of believers.
